findings: The test corpus revision and the 276/217 case counts did not change between the old full-suite log and this run.
Rebuilding dad440e reproduces the same three false positives and seven rejection differences; these are not introduced by the latest four-item implementation.
All three false-positive fixtures pass current Sail in both default and strict-bitvector modes. The individual introducing changes have not been bisected.

The upstream suite enables strict-bitvector; the LSP probe does not model that mode. Earlier declaration checks enforced negative-width restrictions by name, and their replacement deliberately removed that behavior for default-mode semantics.
negative_bits_list is accepted by current Sail in default mode and rejected with strict-bitvector. It must not be fixed by forcing the strict-mode rule on all projects.

The other six rejection differences also fail current Sail in default mode: five undefined/empty-type failures and procstate1 missing a default register value. These are real missing checks, even though their strict-mode first error is different.
Recent historical verification focused on unit tests, RISC-V, and targeted compiler cases; those checks did not preserve the full-suite agreement gate.
next_actions: Fix the three genuine false-positive regressions.
Implement/recover the five undefined/inhabitance checks and the register default-value check.
Make strict-bitvector mode explicit in project semantics and conformance comparison.
Preserve full-suite acceptance/rejection baselines with compiler revision, library revision and flags; keep default and strict results separate.
